name: Example Pipe Fragility Library
description: The Example Pipe Fragility Library is a documented set of fragility functions for buried water mains under earthquake ground motion, giving repair rates per kilometre as a function of peak ground velocity for six pipe materials and three diameter classes. It is compiled by the Example Water Institute, a research body, from published post-event surveys, to support seismic risk assessment of distribution networks. The functions are generic and intended for use anywhere, though the underlying surveys come mostly from North America and Japan between 1971 and 2016. The library is published as a technical report in PDF with the parameters in an accompanying CSV file, free of charge under CC-BY-4.0, without registration. Caveats: the functions do not cover liquefaction-induced displacement separately, and plastic pipes are represented by few observations, so their curves are uncertain. Inputs are ground motion intensity and pipe attributes; outputs are expected repair rates. Simulation uses include hazard exposure and resilience analysis of drinking water systems. No related records are catalogued yet.
